parts.text: A student determines the weight of a metre ruler using a balancing method. Fig. 1.1 shows the set-up. Fig. 1.1

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) The student places the metre ruler on the pivot. She places a load P on the metre ruler at the 90.0 cm mark. She adjusts the position of the metre ruler on the pivot so that the metre ruler is as near as possible to being balanced. The ruler balances with the pivot at the 75.0 cm mark. Calculate the distance a from the 90.0 cm mark to the pivot. Record the value of a in the first row of Table 1.1. [1]

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) She records, in Table 1.1, the distance b from the pivot to the 0.0 cm end of the metre ruler. She repeats the procedure placing the load P at the 85.0 cm mark, 80.0 cm mark, 75.0 cm mark and 70.0 cm mark. She records the values of a and b in Table 1.1. Table 1.1 a / cm b / cm 75.0 13.1 71.9 11.3 68.8 9.4 65.6 7.5 62.5 Plot a graph of a / cm ( y -axis) against b / cm ( x -axis). Start the y -axis at a = 0.0 cm. Start the x -axis at a suitable value for the results. Draw the best-fit line. [4]

ms.label: 1(b)
ms.text:
Graph:
Axes correctly labelled and right way round
Suitable scales
All plots correct to ½ small square
Good line judgement, thin, continuous line

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) Determine the gradient G of the graph. Show clearly on the graph how you obtained the necessary information. G = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(c)
ms.text:
Method shown clearly on graph
Triangle using at least ½ of candidate’s line between extreme plots.

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The weight W of the metre ruler is numerically equal to 2 G . Calculate the weight W of the metre ruler. W = ......................................................... [2]

ms.label: 1(d)
ms.text:
W = 2G with unit N
W in range 1.0–1.4

ms.label: 1(e)
ms.text:
Difficult to obtain exact balance
OR difficult to judge position of (centre of) load
OR load / ruler may slide

ms.label: 1(f)
ms.text: Balance rule on pivot, balance point is at centre of mass / Find where the rule balances.
